cards.explanation: The words of his own mouth did the trapping. The writer says the son has been "…trapped by the words of your lips, ensnared by the words of your mouth…" (Proverbs 6:2). No bandit, no ambush. Just a promise that left his own mouth and came back with teeth.

The word is "humble." The writer says, "Go, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor." (Proverbs 6:3). It's not the easy road, friends. I've had to swallow my pride once or twice, and it goes down like a dry cookie. But it gets the job done.

The answer is False. Nothing in the text says it can wait. The writer says, "Allow no sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids." (Proverbs 6:4). Not a nap, not a little shut-eye, none of it. The pillow will have to wait.

The creature is the ant. The writer says, "Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker; observe its ways and become wise." (Proverbs 6:6). A tiny bug with a big résumé. Somebody get that ant a chef's hat.

The answer is True. The writer says the ant works "Without a commander, without an overseer or ruler…" (Proverbs 6:7). No boss, no clipboard, no whistle. It just gets the work done. That's a better work record than mine.

The ant prepares in summer at harvest time. The writer says it "…prepares its provisions in summer; it gathers its food at harvest." (Proverbs 6:8). It packs the pantry while the getting is good. Smart little thing.

The answer is False. The writer doesn't warn about one long snooze. He says, "A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest…" (Proverbs 6:10). Every one of those is little. They sound harmless, friends, and I think that's the danger.

The word is poverty. The writer says, "…poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit." (Proverbs 6:11). That comes right after "A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest…" (Proverbs 6:10). Little rests on one side, and poverty like a robber on the other.

He talks with his eyes and feet and fingers. He is "…winking his eyes, speaking with his feet, and pointing with his fingers." (Proverbs 6:13). His mouth is perverse and the rest of him joins in. I'd say he's got a full-body conversation going on.
The word is deceit. The writer says, "With deceit in his heart he devises evil…" (Proverbs 6:14). The winking and pointing are only what you see on the outside, friends. The plan is inside.
What he continually sows is discord. The writer says, "he continually sows discord." (Proverbs 6:14). Continually, so it's a habit and not a slip. That's on top of the evil he devises.

Sudden calamity that shatters him is what comes. The writer says, "…calamity will come upon him suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered beyond recovery." (Proverbs 6:15). Suddenly, in an instant. That's how fast the verse says it comes.
The answer is True. Right there in the list is "…a lying tongue…" (Proverbs 6:17). It's number two of the seven that are detestable to Him. The writer didn't hide it in the fine print.

What the first three have in common is that each one is a part of the body. Eyes, tongue and hands are all body parts (Proverbs 6:17). The list keeps going that way, with a heart and feet next (Proverbs 6:18). It's a whole person, head to toe, and the sins are in how each part gets used.
Those feet run swiftly to evil. The writer says "…feet that run swiftly to evil…" (Proverbs 6:18). Fast feet headed the wrong way, friends. Running is great, but not toward that.
